Definition: a risk assessment workflow to combine information required for Next Generation Risk Assessment (NGRA), coined by Animal-free Safety assessment of chemicals: Project cluster for Implementation of novel Strategies (ASPIS; joint collaboration ONTOX, PrecisionTox, RISK-HUNT3R)
Exposure to potentially harmful factors or substances in contaminated food or drinking water

The exposure to potentially harmful chemical, physical, or biological agents in the environment or to environmental factors that may include ionizing radiation, pathogenic organisms, or toxic chemicals.

Term: European Centre for the Validation of Alternative Methods
Definition: The EU Reference Laboratory for alternatives to animal testing, located in Ispra, Italy.

The European Chemicals Agency (ECHA) is responsible for, among other things, implementing European Union legislation on chemicals, such as REACH (Registration, Evaluation, Authorization and Restriction of Chemicals) and CLP (Classification, Labelling and Packaging of substances and mixtures).
The European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) is responsible for providing scientific advice on risks related to food and animal feed throughout the entire supply chain in the European Union.

The measure of all the exposures of an individual from all sources, including environmental and occupational sources, in a lifetime and how those exposures relate to health. (from https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/topics/exposome/ on 06/06/2019)
Contact between a toxicological agent and an outer boundary of an organism.

The process of assessing the magnitude, frequency and duration of exposure of a certain organism to a certain agent; OF the process of assessing the total external (or internal) exposure following one or more exposure/use scenarios that are described in terms of route, extent, frequency and duration of exposure, including exposure via more than one exposure route (aggregated exposure) and exposure to multiple chemicals (cumulative exposure).

The process of assessing the intrinsic hazard a substance poses to human health and/or the environment. This provides information on potential human health effects such that a safe production and use of a chemical can be assured. Two types can be generally distinguished, i.e. with the purpose to classify the chemical to a certain category of toxicity (mostly qualitative assessment) or to derive an exposure limit, such as a health-based guidance value or product limit, that ensures safe use.
First step of risk assessment and management in systematically discovering, recognizing and documenting potential risks which may negatively impact the objectives of an organization or individual
Measurement of the body burden of toxic chemical compounds, elements, or their metabolites, in biological substances

The amount of a chemical (or its active metabolites) present in human tissues or biological fluids over time, typically expressed as concentration-time profiles or dose metrics, resulting from external exposure after ADME/TK processes, and used as the input for the Toxicodynamics/AOP step.
A functional or anatomical change, resulting from the exposure of a living organism to a substance.
Broad class of computational algorithms using random sampling to obtain numerical results
Exposure to a hazard in the workplace
The pharmacological science relating to the collection, detection, assessment, monitoring, and prevention of adverse effects with pharmaceutical product
Differences in measurable biological values, characteristics, or traits, among individuals of a population or between population groups.
The amounts of various substances in the diet recommended by governmental guidelines as needed to sustain healthy life.

Term: The legislation of 'Registration, Evaluation, Authorization and Restriction of Chemicals'
Definition: Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council concerning the Registration, Evaluation, Authorization and Restriction of Chemicals (REACH).
The process of assessing human health and environmental risks in a historic, current or emerging exposure scenario for which a concern has risen.
A process to combine information for a substance about the hazard and exposure to determine how much risk there is.

The overarching term for hazard and risk assessment in toxicology. For pharmaceuticals, this term is generally used for assessments of the safety of a certain application of pharmaceuticals, including the determination of the therapeutic window and risk/benefit analysis.
Observing, recording, or detecting the effects of a chemical substance administered to an individual

Term: WHO Human Health Risk Assessment Toolkit: Chemical Hazards
Definition: A publication that provides guidance on how to identify, gather, and use the information needed to assess chemical hazards, exposures, and related health risks. It was developed by the International Programme on Chemical Safety.
